caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 442 of 2002
lawyer:
Rokanuddin Mahmud, Senior Advocate, instructed by Mvi Md Wahidullah, Advocate-on-Record—For the Petitioners. 
Not represented — The Respondents.
parties:
Abdul Huq and others ------ Petitioners
Vs.
Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh represented by the Secretary, Ministry of Land and others ------ Respondents
full_judgment: 3. The writ-petitioners of Writ Petition No. 105 of 1999 namely Haji Md Abdul Huq, Shabur Rahman and Md Fazlul Haq contend that they purchased land of Plot Nos. 929, 930, 974, 957, 968, 972, 973, 912, 913, 911, Khatian No. 268 JL No. 1426 by registered deed No. 5208 dated 6-9-50, No. 4413 dated 7-6-63, No. 4025 dated 2-1-51, No. 5152 dated 24-6-60 in all more or less 11.40 acres. The petitioners and their brothers have been possessing the land for 38 years by constructing semi-pucca structures therein. Afia Banu, writ-petitioner of Writ Petition No. 2504 of 1999 claimed that she purchased 24 decimals of land of plot No. 737 of Khatian No. 211 of Mouja Bhatara by registered deed No. 6634 dated 11-12-1979 and deed No. 1239 dated 9-11-1976 and has been possessing the same land by constructing two-storied building. The then Dhaka Improvement Trust framed an improvement scheme for development of residential area covering an area of 2760 acres of land in 7 Mouzas. The Dhaka Improvement Trust started acquisition proceeding in respect of the aforesaid land first in LA Case No. 91/57-58 and thereafter in LA Case No. 138/61-62 both under section 93A of the Town Improvement Act, 1953. The possessions of the lands were not taken over from the owners who continued in possession and enjoyed their land. Out of the aforesaid 2760 acres of land so requisitioned, about 343 acres has been utilised by the Dhaka Improvement Trust for the scheme Banani Model Town and the remaining 2417 acres of land were kept for development of Baridhara Residential Scheme. In a meeting held on 15-2-64, the Board of Trustees of Dhaka Improvement Trust decided to revise the scheme and on 17-4-64 decided to acquire only 832 acres and to abandon the remaining land and the Board requested the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka to release the land from requisition falling outside the revised scheme and for acquiring only 832 acres of land vide letter No. DLR/145/L dated 15-7-65. Subsequently, the Government approved the revised scheme by Memo No. DIT/72/65-673-Reqn, dated 6-5-1966 and the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka was directed to vacate the requisition order in respect of the lands outside the scheme. The Dhaka Improvement Trust further reduced the areas of the scheme by bringing down the area of 542 acres i.e., 522 acres in LA Case No. 138/61-62 and 20 acres of LA Case No. 91 of 1957-58 vide Memo No. 49/70/450-Reqn dated 18-6-1970. The Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka was directed to finalise acquisition in respect of 542 acres of land. Accordingly, the Government affirmed its decision for acquisition of land. In August, 1990 the respondent No. 1 purported to do the work of earth filling in some lands of Bhatara Mouza falling in LA Case No. 138 of 1961-62 outside the said 542 acres of land under revised development scheme whereupon some of the affected persons filed writ petitions against such action and Rule nisi was issued by this Court. In 1997, the respondent No. 2 invited tender notice No. 3 of 1977/98 for the purpose of filling up the low land including the land of the petitioners and the tender was published in the daily "Janakantha" on 10-11-1997. The petitioners raised objection to the respondent No. 2 who illegally and arbitrarily invited the tender for filling up the land for which the petitioners would be highly prejudiced. The respondent No. 2 after requisition and acquisition of the property has not made any payment of compensation to the petitioners and the respondent No. 3 has not acquired the land in question through Gazette notification and, therefore, no right has been accrued to the respondent No. 2 and the said tender was invited in violation of the existing pro4isions of law. In the circumstances, the petitioners have sought for direction to release the petitioners' land immediately and to restrain the respondents by an order of injunction from filling up earth in the land of the petitioners.
